checks.detail: AC-3 is not_met (In the realistic overlap, the card shows the right PR and gate: with #48 and #49 open, TRU-6's card shows 'Rollout round 1: pass' (from its real Linear comments) and 'PR #49 checks pass'. That is luck of ordering. A PR is now tied to the first ticket ID in its body as well as its title, and the card takes the first tied PR in GitHub's list order (newest first). Round 1's method served all of booking's real merged PRs as open, and the ticket's own e2e ('a merged pipeline PR and TRU-6's records show on its card') fails under it. TRU-6's card showed PR #52 'Add the PR review stage to the ticket pipeline' (infra/sdlc-pr-review-stage) instead of its pipeline PR #49. TRU-7's card showed #56 'Let the rollout watch be run by hand...' instead of #53. Both were tied only because their bodies mention the ticket in passing. So whether a card shows its own PR depends on whether a newer PR has mentioned the ticket. The unit tests pass and fail against round-1 code, but they never have two PRs naming the same ticket.)

checks.detail: 1 open: crates/server/src/github.rs:56 together with crates/server/src/board.rs:52. A PR is tied to the first TRU-ID found in its title or else its body, and nest() shows prs.iter().find(), the first such PR. bbooth/booking's infra and ci PRs mention tickets in passing in their bodies ('Found while opening TRU-6's PR', 'Run against TRU-6's real PR head'). Observed with real merged PRs served as open: TRU-6's card showed #52 instead of its pipeline PR #49, and TRU-7's card showed #56 instead of #53. The ticket's own e2e therefore fails on real data. Possible fixes: rank title matches (or a branch naming the ticket) above body matches, or require the body to name only that ticket. No test covers two PRs naming one ticket.
